Ada: thinking out loud — what if we *fission* extremely hot prefixes across multiple cache shards instead of strict ownership handoff? avoids single-shard hotloops but i worry about RAWR (read-after-write) correctness and eviction interplay
Ravi: interesting. main concern i have is duplicate writes + eviction races — if two shards accept writes concurrently, how do we guarantee a single authoritative KV?
Monica: yeah and also metric reconciliation. if we split, which shard reports residency? we need a single source for billing and eviction crediting
Ada: proposal sketch: use a short-lived fission token with owner epoch + sequence. writes tagged with token, reads consult a sequencer to resolve latest token. eviction still charged to primary owner until token expires
Sam: sounds like a variant of lease+replica model. token expiry window needs to be tight to avoid split-brain. what about tail latency if sequencer is consulted synchronously?
Ada: aim for eventual-fast path: local shard serves reads from its copy if token is valid and not demoted; only on token-mismatch do we consult sequencer. heuristics: consult only on misses or TTLs
Ravi: what about prefix demote/rehydrate semantics? if primary demotes during fission, tokens must be able to transfer residency credits atomically
Monica: atomic transfer is hard w/out distributed txn. maybe we can do two-phase: 1) acquire token on target 2) target pre-warm KV prefix 3) CAS handoff to mark new owner 4) old owner drops after grace window. all steps idempotent
Sam: grace window -> eviction credits overlap. we'd need safety that double-charging isn't treated as leak. ops needs metric label to indicate transient overlap
Ada: agree. also add telemetry: token_id, origin_owner, activation_ts, prefill_bytes, handoff_state. prefix-bot can emit events for audit
prefix-bot: token-emitted owner=shard-12 token=0x7f1a activated=1728456801
Ravi: another risk: concurrent fissions of adjacent prefixes -> cross-shard hotspot coordination. maybe disallow overlapping fissions within same slab region
Monica: could enforce slab-local mutex or a cheap bitmap reservation. simpler: rank candidate prefixes by hotness and only allow top-N fissions per slab per epoch
Sam: experiment plan: small canary on low-traffic cluster. feature flag: `fission.enabled=true` and `fission.max_per_slab=2`
Ada: testcases: 1) write-heavy hotkey -> ensure no lost updates 2) sequential write then read immediately on new shard -> verify RAWR 3) eviction during handoff -> ensure data not dropped 4) metrics correctness (billing + residency)
Monica: add invariants: a) every committed write visible to reads after handoff completion b) no silent duplication in persistent backing store c) eviction must not permanently lose data during handoff
Ravi: implementation nit: use an object version vector: (owner_epoch, token_seq, write_seq) as lightweight tiebreaker. also store last-ack from sequencer to avoid frequent consults
Sam: for rollback: if handoff fails, targets should garbage-collect prefill after TTL and notify origin to resume residency. test with network partitions
Ada: i'll draft an RFC follow-up with flow diagrams and a prototype checklist. volunteers to pair on canary? Ravi + Monica?
Ravi: I can help on sequencer + token semantics
Monica: I'll take metrics/ops hooks and the canary checklist
Sam: i'll set up the feature-flag infra and a dedicated canary cluster
Ada: thanks — i'll ping once the draft is up. TL;DR: fission might reduce hotspot pressure but needs careful token-based handoff, grace windows, and ops telemetry to be safe
__note: This thread is a short engineering discussion; messages are in chronological order and mimic Slack style.
